name: Pthaha
note: One dot above the letter and one below. Short a, as in bayta. The next consonant is often doubled, as in rabba.

name: Zqapa
note: Two slanted dots above. Long a, as in baba.

name: Zlama, short
note: Two level dots below. Short i, as in libba. The next consonant is often doubled.

name: Zlama, long
note: Two slanted dots below. Long e, as in keka. A plain Yodh after it only lengthens it, as in resha.

name: Khwasa
note: Yodh with a dot below. Long i, as in ilana.

name: Rwasa
note: Waw with a dot below, as in nura.

name: Rwaha
note: Waw with a dot above, as in zora.

name: Rukkakha
note: A small dot below softens a letter: b to w, g to gh, d to dh, k to kh, t to th. Depending on your family’s speech you may say dh and th as plain d and t.

name: Talqana
note: A short line above a letter that is written but not said, as in at, kha and shetta.

name: Syame
note: Two dots above a word mark the plural: malka is a king, malke is kings. Mayya, water, always carries them.

name: Majliyana
effect: a borrowed sound: j, ch or zh
note: A tilde under Gamal, Kap or Shin gives j, ch and zh, mostly in borrowed words.
